title: CPersona recall failure attribution, profile version 1
description: One audited recall failure: the failure code confirmed for it, the evidence the auditor had for that code, the trace it was read from, and, when the recall was replayed, the replay's outcome. Only a caller that knows the answer can confirm a failure, so this record is written outside the server (by a benchmark or a production review), not by the recall. The codes are the failure taxonomy of the 2.6 design (section 8). benchmarks/recall_trace_confirm.py assigns the codes it can establish from a trace and the inputs below and writes this record with attribution_record().

case.description: The auditor's identifier for the failed case (a benchmark question id, a report id). Opaque to this profile.

gold_refs.description: References of the records that hold the answer; any one of them suffices.

inputs.description: Which evidence the auditor passed besides the trace. A code that needs an input is assigned only when the input was passed (CAPTURE_MISS: stored_texts; REPRESENTATION_MISS: stored_texts, quotes and searchable_chars; SYSTEM_DEGRADED: degraded; EVIDENCE_NOISE: shown_by_ref and quotes; RECONSTRUCTION_LOSS and AGENT_MISUSE: the shown text and quotes).

shown_text.description: The text the reader was shown was passed.

quotes.description: The answer's text in the record was passed.

correct.description: Whether the reader answered correctly; null when no reader was run.

stored_texts.description: The stored text of each gold reference was passed.

searchable_chars.description: How much of each gold record semantic search reaches was passed.

shown_by_ref.description: The text shown for each returned record was passed.

degraded.description: Whether the recall ran degraded, as recorded; null when not recorded.

unattributed_reason.description: Why the failure cannot be attributed. Required when code is UNATTRIBUTED, and only then.

trace_digest.description: The first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the trace serialised as JSON with sorted keys and no whitespace, so the record names the exact trace it was read from without carrying it.

code.description: A confirmed failure code. The first twelve are the taxonomy every recall shares; the last eight belong to the recall process (the time cue's loop).

replay.description: The outcome of replaying the recall. `identical` says whether running the recorded request again reproduced what the reader was shown; a code read from a replay that did not reproduce is weaker evidence. A counterfactual replay changes one condition and records the code before and after.

kind.description: The one condition changed: raise the depth, lift a threshold, run one arm alone, change a fusion weight, return the raw evidence instead of the reconstruction, widen the budget, disable a cue, substitute the embedding, run the baseline code, hand the reader the oracle evidence, or re-attribute with a different version of the attribution tool.

value.description: The changed value, in the kind's own terms.
